rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO IMPOSE A FIVE (5)-YEAR TARIFF RATES REDUCTION SCHEME CURRENTLY AT THREE PERCENT (3%) IN THE IMPORTATION OF FOOD AND BEVERAGES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to impose a five (5) year tariff rates reduction scheme currently at three percent (3%) in the importation of food and beverages. The proposed tariff adjustment is expected to maintain the viability of industries and companies that engage in the importation of food and beverages and at the same time protect the thousands of jobs that are dependent on these companies. through the bill, the food and beverage sectors are expected to maintain their viability and improve their performance, thereby rendering an increase in other forms of government revenues like corporate and individual income tax, value-added tax, documentary stamp tax, local business taxes, among others; and providing direct and indirect employment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-02-05

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REDUCE THE CURRENTLY IMPOSED IMPORT DUTIES IN FINISHED MEDICINE AND ON RELATED RAW MATERIALS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Pursuant to this Act, all import duties on finished medicines ccurrently imposed at five (5%) percent shall be REDUCED to three percent (3%); Provided, that the said reduction shall be imposed only for five (5) years upon the effectivity of this Act; Provided, further, that such reduction shall be reviewed after five (5) years of its implementation and two (2) years thereafter to assess whether or not such reduction is indeed serving its purposes and intent. Subject to the stipulations in Section 1 hereof, import duties on raw materials necessary for the manufacture of above-said medicines shall further be reduced from the currently imposed three percent (3%) to one percent(1%).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-02-05

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBER SIX THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED SEVENTY-FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE GENERICS ACTS OF 1988, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Republic Act 6675 which is aimed at ensuring stronger deterrence against dubious profit-oriented pharmaceutical companies and distributors which, like leeches, will continuously suck blood from many of the poor Filipinos.  To protect the public from these elements in the pharmaceutical industry, this proposed legislation attempts to add the following provisions: (1) definition and requirements for quality control standards; and (2) stiffer provision on quality, manufacturer's identity and responsibility.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-02-05

rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill is grounded on the premise that the policy of importing medicines should bring more benefits especially to the Filipino consumers not only in terms of the financial cost of medicines but also their efficacy and safety as well.

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE MANNER OF ELECTION OF THE MEMBERS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE PHILIPPINE VETERANS BANK AND AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND EIGHTEEN AND REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE
rows.abstract: The issue concerns the ELECTION of the members of the board of Directors of the Bank. The veterans and their kins call for a wider REPRESENTATION of the veterans, themselves, in the board. They urge that their voices should be genuinely heard in theannual stockholders meeting.  They are critical of the system of disseminating the notice of the stockholders meeting that, in effect, does not enable all stockholders to be present and vote during the meeting. A remedy has to be prescribed with regard to the impossibility of notifying and gathering in one single place the 510,000 stockholders for the purpose of electing the Board members, the tremendous expenses involved, aside from the problems it will create before, during and after the meetting and elections.

rows.abstract: This bill adds the following power and function of the Sugar Regulatory Administration: To CLASSIFY all sugar produced in, exported from and imported into the Philippines according to such established categories as for export, domestic, reserve andworld market.

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR POLICY REFORMS TO ENSURE THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF SUGAR PLANTERS IN AREAS WHERE THERE IS A SUGAR MILLING MONOPOLY
rows.abstract: "Sugar Planters Policy Reforms Act".  This bill provides policy reforms, such as: (a) A milling contract between sugar central and sugar planter(s) shall be mandatory before each planting season; (b) Government and government-owne d or-controlled financial isntitutions shall provide adequate financing to sugar planters while strenthening the integrity of the quedan system; and (c) Sugar planters assosicaiton dues collected through sugar centrals shall not be withheld by the latter as loan guarantees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-02-05

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING HUMAN CLONING IN THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Cloning Prohibition Act of 2001". This bill declares the policy of the State to value the  dignity of every human person and guarantee full respect for human rights. The State recognizes the sanctity of family life, and is committed to protect andstrenthen the family as a basic autonomous social institution. Towards this end, the government must and shall ban the conduct of human cloning since every human being has intrinsic dignity and worth which must be preserved, respected and safeguarded.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-02-06

rows.author: C118
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AMENDMENTS TO ARTICLE VII, SECTION OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION, AUTHORIZING THE CONDUCT OF A PLEBISCITE IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE XVII, SECTION 4 OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill provides for the following amendment to Article VII, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution: Section 2. No person may be lected President unless he is a natural-born citizen of the Philippines, a registered voter, able to read and write, A DEGREE HOLDER FROM AN ACCREDITED INSTITUTION, at least forty years of age on the day of the election, and a resident of the Philippines for at least ten years immediately preceding such election. AT THE TIME OF THE FILING OF THE CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY, THE CANDIDATE FOR THE POSITION OF PRESIDENT MUST BE OF GOOD MORAL CHARACTER, MUST NOT HAVE BEEN CONVINCED OF ANY CRIME INVOLVING MORAL TURPITUDE, AND MUST HAVE OCCUPIED THE POSITION OF RESPONSIBILITY AND LEADERSHIP IN ANY GOVERNMENT POSITION OR RECCOGNIZED PRIVATE ORGANIZATION."
